PullRequest.Title: Agent Host: gate Copilot Memory (cloud and local) behind settings
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Adds opt-in [Copilot Memory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory) for Copilot SDK (Agent Host) sessions.

### Settings (both off by default)
- `chat.copilot.memory.enabled`: enables cloud memory. Sent as `memory: { enabled }` on every session create and resume. Experiment-capable.
- `chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled`: with memory on, stores memories in `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` via the runtime flag `copilot_swe_agent_memory_in_repo_store`. Changing it restarts the Copilot SDK client after active turns finish, because resident sessions don't reapply feature flags.

Both are forced off when the account disables preview features. Ephemeral sessions, and peer chats under them, never get memory.

### Known limitations (runtime-owned)
- Local memory isn't covered by GitHub's Copilot Memory policies, and doesn't support user-scoped memories or non-GitHub repos.
- The memory file can be included in agent or Agents window commits.
- There's no managed-settings policy key for memory yet.

### How to test
1. Enable `chat.copilot.memory.enabled` in a GitHub repo, ask the agent to remember a convention, and confirm the memory prompt appears.
2. Also enable `chat.copilot.memory.local.enabled` and confirm `.github/copilot-memories.jsonl` is written.

### Validation
- Launcher, settings, startup config and `agentService` unit tests: **passed** (748).
- New and updated `copilotAgent.test.ts` tests: **passed**. The suite's 12 other failures are pre-existing and environment-related.

Scenarios.Scenario: Forward memory and local-memory settings or preview-policy changes into the local Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A setting or account-policy event computes an effective boolean, dispatches a RootConfigChanged action over the existing local Agent Host protocol, updates root state, and persists root configuration. This is on the setting-change path, not chat input/rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one RootConfigChanged patch for each effective key whose structurally compared value changed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per changed Memory or LocalMemory key; unchanged values are suppressed. A policy transition can change both keys, while initial reconciliation only sends missing/different values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two keys and their dispatches did not exist; existing forwarded keys already used the same per-key path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The setting/policy propagation waits only for local dispatch scheduling; it does not block an active turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the merged Agent Host root configuration after RootConfigChanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence request per effective changed key, normally one or two on an explicit setting/policy transition; structural equality prevents steady-state repeats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No persistence was triggered for these absent memory keys; other settings already used the same persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is sequenced by the configuration service and is not on chat turn progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of effective memory-related settings changed in one infrequent user or policy event (maximum two), not number of sessions or chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two key pushes may begin independently, but each is equality-guarded and root writes are serialized by the existing configuration service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root state is the warm cache for forwarded values; structural equality suppresses unchanged dispatches. Persisted root config seeds later host lifetimes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the dispatch, equality guard, state update, and persistence path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact persistence duration is platform-dependent, but cardinality is fixed and events are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff adds at most two bounded, infrequent config updates and does not create collection-scaled or hot-path work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable the in-repository memory store while a Copilot SDK client exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The forwarded root-config event recomputes effective local memory. If it changed, a restart is requested; active turns/subagents finish first, then the single shared client and resident sessions stop. A replacement subprocess starts lazily on the next operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop the shared Copilot runtime and lazily start a replacement with the new startup snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced restart per effective local-store transition, shared across all sessions; concurrent restart reasons are accumulated and concurrent starts share _clientStarting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Memory settings did not trigger a client restart. Existing startup-baked settings already used this same deferred, coalesced lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Never interrupts or delays active turns; a cold replacement start is on the next Copilot operation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the model catalog after stopping the old client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scheduled refresh per applied shared-client restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every existing startup-config restart already cleared and refreshed the catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog refresh is scheduled after teardown and is not awaited by the setting change; the next session may independently ensure the client.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit LocalMemory/effective Memory transition; resident chat count affects teardown breadth but not subprocess restart count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Restart waits for zero busy chats, pending reasons are coalesced in a Set, and client startup is shared through one promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm client is retained when only cloud memory changes or LocalMemory changes while Memory is off. A required effective local-store change invalidates the shared client once; later sessions reuse the replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startup snapshot comparison, active-work gating, reason coalescing, teardown, and shared startup are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold runtime startup cost and number of resident sessions vary, but the trigger is an explicit, infrequent setting/policy transition.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: restart cost is bounded, deferred outside active work, coalesced globally, and required because resident sessions do not reapply this runtime feature flag.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a durable Copilot SDK session with cloud or local memory enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session launch builds configuration, then performs the existing SDK createSession or resumeSession IPC. The diff adds a boolean memory option and local-store feature flag to that same request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume one Copilot SDK session with memory configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing SDK create/resume call per session launch attempt; the diff does not add another call or increase concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/resume call occurred without explicit memory and local-store fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing SDK call remains on session-launch critical path; adding two booleans has negligible serialization cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime-owned cloud memory storage/recall when the opted-in feature is used
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Not visible in this repository; controlled by runtime behavior and only enabled by explicit opt-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Memory was not enabled through Agent Host session configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potential runtime memory service work may occur during turns, but this diff exposes the requested feature rather than adding host-side fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: External Copilot runtime selected by COPILOT_LOCAL_MEMORY_FEATURE_FLAG
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime-owned reads/appends to .github/copilot-memories.jsonl for local memory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Not visible in repository code; applies only when both memory settings are enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Agent Host did not select the runtime's in-repository memory store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime-owned file work may affect memory-enabled turns, but no host-side per-item loop or eager scan is introduced here.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session launch/resume and subsequent explicitly opted-in memory usage; no repository collection is looped over by changed host code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing launcher behavior applies; independent config preparation is already grouped with Promise.all, and the diff adds no new concurrent operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runtime owns cloud/local memory caching and persistence; host configuration is read once per launch. Warm resident sessions reuse the existing runtime until an effective local-store transition requires restart.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged host boundary cardinality; limited for runtime-internal costs because implementation is external.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external runtime's memory lookup/write frequency and cache implementation are not present in this repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: enabling a requested opt-in feature may incur its inherent runtime work, but the diff does not demonstrate avoidable fan-out, repeated host work, or an unbounded host allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a peer chat under an ephemeral session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentService performs one O(1) ephemeral-state lookup, passes the flag through chat creation, and the launcher explicitly disables memory before the existing SDK create/resume call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing provider chat creation and SDK create/resume with memory disabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider call and one existing SDK launch per peer chat; no additional boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Peer creation already crossed these boundaries, but ephemeral ownership was not propagated to the Copilot launch plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added state lookup and boolean serialization are negligible; disabling memory avoids runtime network/filesystem work for ephemeral peers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user-created ephemeral peer chats; each independently follows the existing one-launch path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Creation remains serialized by the existing per-session/per-chat queues in CopilotAgent; the diff adds no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ephemeral state is read from the in-memory state manager. No memory cache/store is initialized because the launch config explicitly disables it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: state lookup, option propagation, and launch-time memory gate are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism; lookup and payload growth are constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the change prevents heavyweight memory behavior on ephemeral peers without adding an expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced setting/policy forwarding, root persistence, deferred shared-client restart, durable session launch/resume, runtime-owned memory boundaries, and ephemeral peer creation. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped regression fix requiring blame.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
